title: Verify the whole verifier-snapshot lock holds before the verifier runs
summary: Root cause: `Snapshot::lock` in crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs treats the lock as held after probing only two places (creating a file at the root, appending to .git/HEAD). The immutable attribute is applied best-effort with `chattr -R`, so a partial lock can pass the probe while other paths (objects, refs, work-tree files) stay writable. The verifier can then change HEAD or the tree, as in jobs 20261015-031159-xx7n and 20261015-033631-x3a1. The fix makes the lock check every directory and file in the tree and fail if any accepts a write, so a verifier never starts on a partly locked snapshot. The audience is the Athena operator, who gets verdicts that are not wrongly voided.

defaults_applied.how: The fix is in `Snapshot::lock`, which all snapshot locking goes through, not in one job's verifier run.
A new test fails on the old lock and passes on the new one. fmt, clippy and test must pass.
One focused change to the lock check and its tests.
Criteria check that a partly locked snapshot is refused, not that a function exists.
The check behind the work is that a snapshot reported as locked refuses writes everywhere.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs (`Snapshot::lock`, `probe_write`, `set_tree_writable`, `set_immutable`, `work_tree_tree`, and the tests at about lines 755-790) and crates/athena-core/src/run/verification.rs (the verifier loop at about lines 198-346 locks, invokes, unlocks, compares HEAD and tree to `prepared`, and reruns once). The entry point is `verification.rs` calling `vsnap.lock()` before `invoke_and_record`. The change adds no record or data file under crates/, so no `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` or round-trip test is involved. The property is measured directly, by attempting writes at every path of a real locked snapshot rather than through a stand-in.
Environment: none. The change is local code and tests. It touches no CI workflow, push or PR, and no records or history reads.

The rerun-once and tree-comparison logic in verification.rs already exists and stays as it is. The leftover cause is that `lock()` can report success while part of the snapshot is still writable, so the fix belongs in `lock()`.

Job 20261015-031159-xx7n (the firstmate explainer rating) was rejected only because of the snapshot-change blocker. Its minor and nit findings about the page content are not addressed here. Its candidate files (CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/explainer-site.md, studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json, xtask/src/site.rs) are dropped from this change. Job 20261015-033631-x3a1 was a retry with the same blocker. Its candidate files (the four above plus studies/firstmate-work-handling/findings.json and model.json) are also dropped. The retry of those content jobs is separate work.

Tests must run as whatever user the test runner is. A test of the new check should make part of the tree writable after a partial lock, for example by restoring a write bit on one nested directory or file, and assert that the check reports it. It must not depend on `chattr` being available.

acceptance_criteria.text: The `lock()` doc comment or the CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entry names the root cause: a lock probed at only two places can be taken for held while other paths in the snapshot remain writable, so the verifier could change its snapshot.

In crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs, `Snapshot::lock` checks every directory and file under the snapshot, `.git` included, with a check that writes nothing permanent. The check does not stop at the first two probes. If any path would accept a write, `lock()` unlocks and returns an error naming that path.

Run `cargo test -p athena-git`. A new test partly unlocks a nested directory or file of a locked snapshot, or simulates a partial lock, and asserts the full-tree check reports that path. The test fails when `lock()` is reverted to the two-place probe and passes with the change. It does not rely on `chattr`.

Run `cargo test -p athena-git` and `cargo test -p athena-core`. The existing tests pass: `a_locked_snapshot_refuses_edits_and_commits_and_keeps_head_and_tree` in athena-git and the snapshot-change rerun tests in crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. All pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an [Unreleased] entry describing the fix, since it is a user-visible change in verification behavior.

out_of_scope: Retrying the firstmate explainer content: studies/firstmate-work-handling/*, xtask/src/site.rs, docs/design/explainer-site.md. The earlier candidates' changes to these files are dropped.
Changing the rerun-once policy or the tree comparison in verification.rs, except to surface a lock failure.
Hashing gitignored files such as target/ in the before/after fingerprint.
Changes to records/, governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) or prompts.
departures: The reference forecast is kept. The change touches a safety-critical lock, which slightly lowers the chance of verification passing, and I expect a modest cost because the area is already well tested.
urgent_reason: It cuts rejected attempts and redo work: two jobs (20261015-031159-xx7n and 20261015-033631-x3a1) were rejected because the verifier changed its snapshot.
hard_reason: It changes the lock that guards the verifier's snapshot, which is part of the verification pipeline and the gate that judges other jobs, so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
